c.tagline: Navarre's walled city of San Fermín, bull-running, and Basque-inspired pintxos.

taxi.fareNote: Metered white taxis; ride-hailing is limited, with Cabify the main app. Fares and hotel prices rise sharply during the San Fermín festival in July.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire and ambulance.

avoid.reason: During San Fermín the Casco Viejo fills with drunken crowds and pickpockets, so secure valuables and skip dark side streets late.

hood_desc: The medieval walled old town and heart of San Fermín, packed with the cathedral, Plaza del Castillo, the Calle Estafeta bull-run route, and pintxo bars. The best base for first-timers and nightlife.
The elegant 19th- and 20th-century grid south of the old town, with boulevards, boutiques, the Ciudadela park edge, and upscale dining. Good for shopping and a refined stay.
A leafy, largely residential district west of the centre around the Yamaguchi park and university, calm and local. Suits families and longer stays.
A traditional neighborhood in the river bend below the walls, increasingly gentrified, with riverside walks along the Arga. Good for a local, budget-friendly feel.
A modern residential area near the university and Navarra hospital, full of everyday shops, cafes, and green space. Quiet and practical, away from the tourist core.
lodging: Hotel Pompaelo Plaza del Ayuntamiento & Spa

water.note: Tap water is safe and excellent quality.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 11 PM, with a limited night-bus network on weekends.
transit.note: Pamplona has no metro or tram; the villavesa city buses (run by TCC) cover the city and its metro area. The walled old town is small and best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash or tap a contactless bank card; a rechargeable travel card offers cheaper fares.

bus: ALSA & Conda intercity coaches from Pamplona bus station
train: Renfe services to Madrid, Zaragoza, Barcelona & San Sebastián from Pamplona station

transit.m: Taxi to city centre (~15 min; there is no regular airport bus)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill for good service is appreciated but not required.

landmarks: Plaza del Castillo
Pamplona's elegant living room, a vast arcaded square ringed by belle-époque cafés like Hemingway's beloved Café Iruña and crowned by a bandstand kiosk.
Catedral de Santa María la Real
A Gothic cathedral hiding behind a neoclassical facade, sheltering France's finest cloister rival, royal tombs and the Occidens museum of city history.
Ciudadela de Pamplona
A star-shaped 16th-century Renaissance fortress commissioned by Philip II, its grassy bastions and moats now a beloved park dotted with contemporary sculpture.
Murallas de Pamplona & Portal de Francia
Among Europe's best-preserved Renaissance city walls, five kilometers of ramparts whose 16th-century French Gate still bears its original drawbridge.
Calle Estafeta
The legendary straightaway of the San Fermín bull run, a narrow bar-lined street that turns into six seconds of adrenaline each July morning.
Monumento al Encierro
A dramatic life-sized bronze freezing the running of the bulls mid-stampede, letting visitors pose among hurtling steers and sprawling runners year-round.
Casa Consistorial (City Hall)
The flamboyant Baroque-facade town hall where the txupinazo rocket launches San Fermín each July 6, unleashing a week of white-and-red revelry.
Museo de Navarra
The region's premier museum, in a former hospital, spanning Roman mosaics, the Romanesque Leyre casket and a portrait by Francisco de Goya.
Parque de la Taconera
Pamplona's oldest and most romantic gardens, where deer, peacocks and pheasants roam the moats beneath Versailles-style flowerbeds and centuries-old fortifications.
Plaza de Toros de Pamplona
One of the world's largest bullrings, the terminus of the encierro, fronted by a bust of Ernest Hemingway, the fiesta's most famous devotee.

train.note: No international trains. Direct Renfe services link Pamplona with Madrid in about 3 hours, Zaragoza in 2, Barcelona and San Sebastián/Donostia; the station sits northwest of the centre with a bus link into town. For France you travel via Irún/Hendaye and change onto SNCF. Booking opens around 60 days ahead - trains sell out completely around San Fermín in July.

bus.note: The underground bus station beside the Ciudadela is central and modern. ALSA (https://www.alsa.com/en) and Conda run frequent coaches to San Sebastián (about an hour), Bilbao (2 hours), Zaragoza, Madrid (5 hours) and Camino de Santiago towns, plus seasonal buses to nearby mountain and ski areas. Book far ahead for San Fermín week.

ferry.note: Pamplona is inland in Navarre with no navigable water, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Olite
half.blurb: A fairytale medieval town 40 minutes south crowned by the Royal Palace of Olite, one of Navarre's finest Gothic castles.

half.name: Puente la Reina
half.blurb: A classic Camino de Santiago town 25 km southwest with a famous Romanesque pilgrim bridge over the Arga.

full.name: Bardenas Reales
full.blurb: A semi-desert badlands natural park of eroded clay ridges about 1h30 south, popular for driving, cycling and film shoots.

full.name: San Sebastián
full.blurb: The elegant Basque coastal city with La Concha beach and world-class pintxos, about an hour north.

full.name: Roncesvalles
full.blurb: The Pyrenean pass and monastery where the French Camino de Santiago enters Spain, around an hour north.
